task:
Build a small single-page web app in the current directory: a Pomodoro focus timer.

Requirements:
- Files: index.html, styles.css, app.js (no frameworks, no CDNs, no build step).
- 25-minute focus / 5-minute break modes with tabs to switch between them.
- Big mm:ss countdown inside an animated circular SVG progress ring.
- Start / Pause / Reset buttons; the Space key toggles start/pause.
- A "sessions completed today" counter that persists in localStorage.
- A polished, modern dark UI that looks good from 360px to 1440px wide.

Work directly in the files. When finished, reply with a one-line summary.

This directory contains a small expense tracker (index.html, styles.css, app.js). Users have reported these problems: 1. Entering 12.50 as the amount saves the expense as $12.00. 2. Deleting an expense sometimes removes a different one, especially with a category filter on. 3. All expenses are gone after reloading the page, although the app is meant to save them. 4. With a category filter on, the total doesn't match the expenses shown. 5. A description like lunch shows up in bold instead of exactly as typed. 6. The newest expenses should be at the top of the list, but they are at the bottom. 7. You can add an expense with a zero or negative amount. That should show the error message instead. Fix all of them in place. Keep everything that already works working: the form, the category filter, the per-category totals and the styling. Keep the existing element ids and classes, because other code depends on them. Don't rewrite the app from scratch. When finished, reply with a one-line summary.

Build a mini spreadsheet as a single-page web app in the current directory: index.html, styles.css and app.js. No frameworks, no CDNs, no build step, and no eval() or new Function(): write your own formula parser.

Grid
- 8 columns (A–H) by 12 rows (1–12), with column letters and row numbers as headers.
- Every cell is an <input> with a data-cell attribute holding its address, e.g. <input data-cell="B3">.
- A cell that is not being edited shows its computed value. When focused it shows the raw content that was entered (e.g. "=A1+1").
- An edit is committed on Enter or when the cell loses focus. Enter also moves focus to the cell below.

Values and formulas
- A cell holds a number, text, or a formula starting with "=".
- Formulas support numbers, cell references (case-insensitive: A1 or a1), + - * / with the usual precedence, unary minus, parentheses, and the functions SUM, AVG and MAX. Functions take ranges (A1:A5), comma-separated arguments (SUM(A1, B2, 3)), or a mix.
- Empty cells count as 0. Using a text cell in arithmetic is an error.
- Results show no floating-point noise: =0.1+0.2 shows 0.3.
- Changing a cell recalculates every cell that depends on it, directly or through other cells.

Errors (shown in the cell instead of a value)
- #DIV/0! for division by zero.
- #REF! for a reference outside A1:H12.
- #CIRC! for a circular reference, shown in every cell of the cycle.
- #ERR! for anything else that can't be parsed or evaluated.
- A formula that uses a cell holding an error also shows an error.

Also
- The sheet is saved in localStorage and restored on reload.
- A "Clear" button empties every cell and the saved sheet.
- Clean, readable styling.

When finished, reply with a one-line summary.

data.json in the current directory holds 137 customer records (fields: id, name, city, signup, orders, spend). Build a single-page data explorer for it: index.html, styles.css and app.js. No frameworks, no CDNs, no build step. Load data.json with fetch, and do not modify it.

Table
- A <table> with one row per record and these columns, in this order: Name, City, Signup date, Orders, Spend.
- Spend shows as US dollars with two decimals and thousands separators (e.g. $1,234.50). Dates show as YYYY-MM-DD.
- A <tfoot> row shows the total Orders and total Spend of all rows that match the current search (not just the current page).

Sorting
- Clicking a column header sorts by that column ascending; clicking the same header again sorts descending.
- Numbers sort numerically, dates chronologically, and text case-insensitively.
- Ties are ordered by id ascending, in both directions.
- The sorted header has aria-sort="ascending" or aria-sort="descending".

Search and pages
- A search box (<input type="search">) filters rows. A row matches when the query appears, ignoring case, in its name or city.
- 10 rows per page, with Previous and Next buttons and a page-size <select> offering 10, 25 and 50.
- A status line reads exactly like "Showing 11–20 of 137" (with an en dash). It reflects the search, so 7 matches give "Showing 1–7 of 7".
- With no matches, show "No results" and no data rows.
- Changing the search or the page size goes back to page 1.

URL state
- The current sort column, direction, search, page and page size are kept in the URL hash, using the keys sort, dir, q, page and size, e.g. #sort=spend&dir=desc&q=ber&page=2&size=25. Sort values are name, city, signup, orders and spend.
- Opening the page with such a hash restores that exact state.

Styling
- Clean and readable. On narrow screens the table scrolls sideways inside its own container instead of making the whole page scroll.

When finished, reply with a one-line summary.

With a category filter on, the total doesn't match the expenses shown. 5. A description like lunch shows up in bold instead of exactly as typed. 6. The newest expenses should be at the top of the list, but they are at the bottom. 7. You can add an expense with a zero or negative amount. That should show the error message instead. Fix all of them in place. Keep everything that already works working: the form, the category filter, the per-category totals and the styling. Keep the existing element ids and classes, because other code depends on them. Don't rewrite the app from scratch. When finished, reply with a one-line summary.
